title: Tool input conformance cases
description: Driven through EACH side's real tool validator: Kioku::Mcp::Validators::* on the host and the Rails request boundary in the core. Both must reach the same outcome and the same wire code. `service_expect` names an additional obligation on the core's use case, because some of these divergences are only visible past validation.
patch_semantics: body_patch is merged over the named base body one level deep; a nested object replaces outright. body_delete removes keys entirely. envelope_patch and envelope_delete apply the same way to the body's envelope.

body.title: Use template0 for the application database
body.body: The ParadeDB image seeds template1 with nine extensions, so the application database must be created from template0.

body.title: Prefer an explicit database template
body.body: Create application databases from a known template rather than inheriting whatever the image seeded.

applicability.conditions: PostgreSQL images that preload extensions into template1

body.reason: The cited compose file no longer sets POSTGRES_DB.

cases.why: The baseline every remember refusal is measured against.
The published envelope accepts expected_revision, but with memory_key refused no caller could name the memory it applies to. Appending a revision was unreachable through the published surface.
Naming an existing memory without declaring the revision you observed is a blind append: the head could have moved and the write would not conflict.
Assistant-authored global records default to proposed and must be able to say so. The core already takes lifecycle; only the host's permitted list made it unreachable.
superseded and retracted are reached by the core through supersession and deletion. A caller asserting them would retract a record by writing a word.

mandatory is user authority only, which is a decision the core makes about the actor - not a reason to refuse the field at the schema. Refusing it at the host made kioku.authority_violation unreachable.

override is what CLAUDE.md's first implementation slice needs. Until implemented.json flips it, the refusal names the field and says why, so a caller never believes an exception was recorded. Flipping the entry turns this case into an acceptance.

override.replacement_body: This project pins the template explicitly.
override.reason: Local exception to the shared preference.

cases.why: The contract's ref is {evidence_key|object_key|event_key}. The core refused anything but object_key with kioku.invalid_request, which told a caller its request was malformed when it was exactly what the contract names.

service_expect.note: A well-formed ref this build cannot resolve is reported per entry, never as a malformed request and never silently dropped from the eligibility count.

cases.why: Only an EMPTY eligible set fails, and it fails with kioku.evidence_required rather than kioku.invalid_request. The companion that stops the case above being satisfied by accepting every ref.
Exactly one of the three. Two keys is an ambiguous reference the core would have to guess at, and the host accepted any non-empty object.
An empty object names nothing.
The contract names a dedicated code for a write that supplied no evidence link, and a caller branches on it differently: it must add evidence, not fix its request.
A reusable statement with no declared limits is not reusable.
An absent binding is never read as permission to write globally.
A save records a conclusion; it never establishes support. claim_support is core-derived and has no input property anywhere in the artifact.
The bypass a top-level name check misses. Closure at every depth is what refuses it; a list of names checked at one level is not.
saved is the durability claim the core makes after canonical commit. A caller must not be able to name it at all.
query is required when mode=lexical. Without it there is nothing to rank.
Embeddings are out of scope, not deferred. The value is permanently unsupported rather than absent, so a caller is told the mechanism does not exist instead of being told to fix its spelling.
Same, for the second removed mechanism.
contracts.json open_decisions requires the alias to be exercised by a fixture before release. It must expand to a mechanism plus a subject route, not become a fourth mechanism.
Two hops is the contract maximum for explicit relationship queries. Three is a request for a mechanism that does not exist.
The edge vocabulary is closed and a name outside it is an unsupported operation, not a typo to be ignored.
edge_kinds is required rather than defaulted so that no call can request an untyped walk.
The batch bound is 1..50. An empty batch is not a fetch.
A dispute must name what was actually disputed. A head pointer moves, and the objection would silently re-target.
The eight operations are the whole surface; context_task is not an arbitrary command interface.

Only close can move the projection to completed_in_scope, against a still-applicable assessment receipt and matching heads. A checkpoint asserting it would let an agent complete a task by writing a word.
The companion that stops the case above being satisfied by refusing every checkpoint state.
